title: Risk Register Update: Hazira gas terminal release and fire, 2020
audience: Enterprise risk management: ERM leads, risk owners and insurers' risk engineers
status: Learning purposes: not a statutory document. Draft learnings from a ProbeMatrix investigation export; validate them before adoption.

data_quality.text: Draft learnings from an unreviewed analysis: the export's Investigation Status is in_progress and no finding is marked as edited by a person, so this pack stays a draft until the investigation is completed and reviewed.

bottom_line.text: Add the threat of a non-specified seal on the 1986 metering skid: the original gasket was replaced by locally bought O-rings as regular practice, with no record of who decided it.
Revisit the rating of the emergency isolation controls: the plan gave no isolation criteria or authority, and the isolation valves could be closed only by hand inside the vapour cloud.
Revisit the rating of management of change: the procedure was published in 2016 but not used after 2018.
Twelve external-audit actions were carried past their dates without the approval the procedure requires: record them as risks accepted without authority.
Add key risk indicators for repeat failures, overdue integrity inspections and changes made without an MOC record, so the register shows these conditions before the next event.

items.text: Proposals for the risk owner to assess: no loss estimates and no rating decisions.

items.risk: Loss of containment at the gas metering skid
items.current_assumption: A seal change on the meter is routine maintenance with no risk of its own.
items.evidence_says: The same meter had its gasket changed in February 2019 and September 2019, and the joint leaked again within a year [EVD-1494]; the malfunction notification raised in September 2020 was not closed after the job [EVD-0591]. The recurrence was never assessed as a risk.
items.proposed_change: Add repeat seal failure on ageing pressure-boundary equipment as a threat to this risk, with the reliability review that should follow a second failure as its control.

items.risk: Escalation of a major hydrocarbon release
items.current_assumption: Emergency isolation valves can be reached and closed by hand during a release.
items.evidence_says: The isolation valves had no remote operation from the control room [EVD-3932]; the shift in-charge had to reach the gas terminal gate before the first valve was closed, 46 minutes after first detection [EVD-9612].
items.proposed_change: Add a vapour cloud that denies access to manual isolation as a threat, and review whether remote or automatic isolation is needed as its control.

items.risk: Escalation of a major hydrocarbon release
items.current_assumption: Anyone who sees a release can warn the operating control room at once.
items.evidence_says: Perimeter security staff saw the vapour first but could tell only the CCTV control room and the main gate; the gas terminal control room heard of it after a further check by camera [EVD-6234] [EVD-8871].
items.proposed_change: Add an indirect warning path from the people most likely to see a release as a threat to early response.

items.current_assumption: Changes to plant and materials go through the management-of-change procedure published in August 2016.
items.evidence_says: The procedure was not followed for changes in 2013 and 2018, and no MOC had been carried out since 2018 [EVD-2986]; the seal substitution never reached a change review [EVD-8645].
items.proposed_change: Reassess the rating of the MOC control against its actual use since 2018, not against the existence of the procedure.

items.risk: Escalation of a major hydrocarbon release
items.current_assumption: The on-site disaster management plan and the ERDMP control the major-leak scenario.
items.evidence_says: Both documents named hydrocarbon leakage but neither gave isolation or stoppage criteria, nor who may decide to isolate [EVD-4052] [EVD-6414].
items.proposed_change: Revisit the rating of the emergency plan as a control for this scenario until it holds isolation criteria and the authority to act on them.

items.risk: Escalation of a major hydrocarbon release
items.current_assumption: Fixed gas detection protects the plant when a release occurs.
items.evidence_says: The detectors were wired to an annunciator for display only, with no automatic shutdown or fire suppression [EVD-8657] [EVD-3452].
items.proposed_change: Rate gas detection as an alarm that depends on people acting, not as an automatic protective control, and review the threats it is credited against.

items.current_assumption: Electrical equipment in the hazardous area keeps its flameproof protection.
items.evidence_says: A flameproof lamp had three bolts missing and its glass case open by 5 to 6 cm [EVD-6916]; electrical maintenance was skewed towards breakdowns, and the post-incident audit was one generic page [EVD-0496] [EVD-9999].
items.proposed_change: Reassess the rating of hazardous-area ignition control against inspection records for the fittings, not against the equipment's certification.

items.risk: Loss of containment from pipeline wall loss
items.current_assumption: Thickness surveys find wall loss and the findings are acted on.
items.evidence_says: The 2017 report found pipes needing corrective action, and three years later no plan existed [EVD-5527]; 1.03 mm of pitted wall loss on a segment with no corrosion allowance was treated with paint [EVD-2397].
items.proposed_change: Reassess the integrity control's rating on whether findings are closed, not on whether surveys are done.

items.current_assumption: The diesel fire-water pumps back up the electric pumps.
items.evidence_says: Of four diesel pumps, two were under maintenance, one ran for 30 minutes and one tripped after two minutes, with no cause found or action recorded [EVD-2432]. The electric pumps carried the incident.
items.proposed_change: Revisit the rating of the fire-water backup against the diesel pumps' recorded availability.

items.risk: Loss of containment at the gas metering skid
items.current_assumption: Parts on a hydrocarbon pressure boundary match the original specification, or a change is approved.
items.evidence_says: The original gasket specification was lost; locally bought O-rings were used as regular practice with no specification or quality check, and there is no record of the date or the authority of the decision to switch [EVD-8645].
items.proposed_change: Record the substitute seal as a risk carried without an approval, and ask the risk owner to decide whether it is accepted, changed or stopped.

items.risk: Open safety actions from the 2018 external audit
items.current_assumption: Audit actions are closed by their dates, or an extension is approved as the procedure requires.
items.evidence_says: 296 of 308 recommendations were complied with; the other 12 had dates extended to 30 April 2021 with no record of the approval the procedure requires [EVD-6852].
items.proposed_change: List each extended action as a risk carried without authority until the required approval is recorded or the action is closed.

items.risk: Loss of containment from pipeline wall loss
items.current_assumption: The four-year thickness-measurement cycle is kept.
items.evidence_says: The last two surveys were in 2011 and 2017, a six-year gap [EVD-8307], and baseline thickness data and pipe schedules were missing for many gas terminal pipes [EVD-8287].
items.proposed_change: Add an indicator of integrity inspections overdue against their cycle, reported with the risk.

items.current_assumption: Every hazardous job has a permit and a job safety plan on record.
items.evidence_says: Some work permits were missing with no record kept of them, and job safety plans were not attached in SAP [EVD-5105].
items.proposed_change: Add an indicator of permits not accounted for and jobs with no job safety plan, reported with the risk.

items.name: Repeat failures on safety-critical equipment
items.measure: Count of second and later failures of the same item within 24 months, from the maintenance notification history.
items.deterioration: Any item with a third failure and no reliability review on record.

items.name: Integrity inspections overdue
items.measure: Share of thickness and integrity inspections past their scheduled cycle, from the inspection plan.
items.deterioration: Any inspection more than one cycle overdue.

items.name: Inspection findings without a corrective plan
items.measure: Number and age of inspection findings that call for corrective action and have no approved plan.
items.deterioration: A finding open across two survey cycles, or closed by a coating where wall loss was found.

items.name: Changes with an MOC record
items.measure: Share of material, equipment and setting changes in the work-order system that carry an MOC record.
items.deterioration: No MOC record raised in a quarter in which changes were made.

items.name: Fire-water pump availability
items.measure: Share of time each fire-water pump is available, from test runs and maintenance records.
items.deterioration: A pump out of service, or a trip with no cause found, beyond the period the site allows.

items.name: Audit actions past their date
items.measure: Number of audit actions past their target date, and how many of the extensions carry the required approval.
items.deterioration: Any extension with no approval on record.

items.failure_mode: No gasket specification was held for the 1986 meter, so locally bought O-rings with no specification or quality check were the regular substitute (L4).
items.fix: Hold the specification for each pressure-boundary seal and block the issue of parts without one.

lint_ok.reason: the administrative change is the system fix at the level of the cause: a held specification and a stores block on unspecified parts

items.failure_mode: The MOC procedure existed but was not used after 2018, so the seal substitution never reached an engineering review (L4).
items.fix: Raise an MOC from the work-order and stores systems whenever a part differs from its specification.

lint_ok.reason: the administrative change is the system fix at the level of the cause: the MOC trigger is built into the work-order and stores systems

items.failure_mode: No test to design pressure was required or done after the September 2020 gasket change, and no procedure covered the return to service (L3).
items.fix: Make a recorded pressure test a hold point before a pressure-boundary item returns to service.

lint_ok.reason: the administrative change is the system fix at the level of the cause: a recorded test as a hold point before return to service

items.barrier: inspection and integrity (acting on inspection results)
items.failure_mode: Wall loss was measured but not acted on for three years, and painting was used for pitted wall loss (L4, L3).
items.fix: Require a fitness-for-service decision on every wall-loss finding, with the risk owner told of any finding left open.

lint_ok.reason: the administrative change is the system fix at the level of the cause: a fitness-for-service decision on every wall-loss finding

items.failure_mode: Gas detection lit an annunciator but started no shutdown or suppression (L4).
items.fix: Link confirmed gas detection to automatic shutdown and fire suppression.

items.failure_mode: The isolation valves could be closed only by hand at the valve; the first was closed 46 minutes after first detection (L4).
items.fix: Provide remote isolation from the control room for the valves that isolate the metering skid.

items.failure_mode: The emergency plans named the leak scenario but gave no isolation criteria and no delegated authority to isolate (L4).
items.fix: Write isolation criteria into the emergency plans and delegate the authority to the control-room role on shift.

lint_ok.reason: the administrative change is the system fix at the level of the cause: isolation criteria and delegated authority written into the plans

items.failure_mode: A flameproof lamp with three bolts missing and its glass case open stayed in service under breakdown-led electrical maintenance (L4, L3).
items.fix: Schedule detailed inspection of every hazardous-area fitting and record each one's state.

lint_ok.reason: the administrative change is the system fix at the level of the cause: a scheduled detailed inspection of every hazardous-area fitting

items.failure_mode: The electric pumps carried the fire cooling. Latent: three of four diesel pumps were under maintenance or tripping, with no cause found (L4, L3).
items.fix: Restore the diesel pumps and find the cause of the trip before the backup is counted again.

limits: The export holds no cost, loss or insurance data, so this pack gives no loss estimate and no cost figure.
The pack proposes changes; it rates no risk and decides nothing. Ratings, acceptance and every decision stay with the risk owner, who fills the risk_owner_decision column of the CSV.
The organisation's risk register and bow-ties were not available to this analysis, so each risk is named plainly rather than by its register id.
The analysis is a desk review of the published enquiry report; it had no access to the site's risk assessments or interviews.
